html:
The Tembé are a Tupi-Guarani people of northeastern Pará and western Maranhão in Brazil, living mainly along the Gurupi and Guamá rivers. With the Guajajara they form the Tenetehara, one people split in two by migration in the 1800s.

They farm manioc and hunt and fish in the forest. Their neighbours include the Ka'apor and the small Anambé people. Since the late 1900s the Tembé of the Alto Rio Guamá reserve have fought loggers, ranchers and settlers who invaded their land, at times seizing and expelling them on their own.
